statements.text: A circle can be drawn (identified) with given terms: 1. the center of the circle.
A circle can be drawn (identified) with given terms: 2. the radius length of the circle.
Construction step 1: take any chosen point as M on the same plane.
Construction step 2: place the tip of the compass at M and with an opening equal to MA draw the circle M. The circle M passes through point A.
Construction step 3: place the tip of the compass at another point M₁ and with an opening equal to M₁A draw circle M₁. The circle M₁ passes through point A.
Construction step 4: repeat the previous work and note the following.
For each chosen point (center of the circle) it is possible to draw a circle passing through point A.
An infinite number of circles can be drawn passing through a given point such as A.
If the radii of these circles are equal in length, then their centers are located on a congruent circle whose center is point A.
Draw the straight segment AB.
Draw the straight line L, the axis of AB, where L ∩ AB = {F} (the center of the circle is on the axis of the chord AB).
Take any chosen point M where M ∈ L, put the tip of the compass at M and with an opening equal to MA draw circle M; it passes through point B.
Put the tip of the compass at another point M1 where M1 ∈ L, and with an opening equal to M1A draw circle M1; it passes through point B.
Repeat the previous work and note:
For each chosen point E on the axis of AB (center of the circle), it is possible to draw a circle passing through the two points A and B.
An infinite number of circles can be drawn to pass through two given points like A and B.
The radius of the smallest circle that can be drawn to pass through the two points A and B equals half the length of AB. Formula: $\frac{1}{2}\overline{AB}$
Two circles cannot intersect in more than two points.
Construction:
Draw the straight line $L_1$, the axis of $\overline{AB}$, thus $M \in L_1$.
Draw the straight line $L_2$, the axis of $\overline{BC}$, thus $M \in L_2$.
If $L_1 \cap L_2 = \{M\}$, place the tip of the compass at point M with an opening equalling MA. Draw the circle M. You will find it passing through the two points B and C.
If A, B and C are collinear then $L_1 \parallel L_2$ and $L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$. Formula: $L_1 \parallel L_2, L_1 \cap L_2 = \phi$
A circle cannot be drawn passing through the three points A, B and C (when collinear).
There is one and only one circle which passes through three noncollinear points.
The circle which passes through the vertices of a triangle is called the circumcircle of this triangle.
A triangle is said to be inscribed in a circle if its vertices are on the circle.
The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect at a point which is the center of the circumcircle of the triangle.
Circumcircle
